mc:handbooktext-bowl: See Meal making guide. Fill by rightmouse clicking on a cooking pot, crock, bucket, or other container with food or liquid inside. If you want to empty a bowl or cooking pot without eating the contents, simply toss it in some water!
mc:handbooktext-crock: Cooking pots, crocks, and bowls can have portions removed or added by placing them on the ground, and then clicking on them with another container. Additionally, when on the ground crocks can be sealed by clicking on them with wax or fat. Both of these actions can also be done when the crock is on a shelf or within the inventory management screen.

mc:handbooktext-potcapacity: Cooking capacity varies by metal. Earlier metals typically fill four matching crocks: Copper and Bismuth 20 servings; Brass and Nickel 28; Cupronickel and Electrum 32; Silver and Gold 36. Iron 28; Meteoric iron 30; Steel 32; Titanium 36 servings per cooking pot.
mc:handbooktext-crockcapacity: Crock capacity varies by metal: Copper and Bismuth 5 servings; Brass and Nickel 7; Cupronickel and Electrum 8; Silver and Gold 9. Crock and pot capacities may differ by metal. Iron 8; Meteoric iron 9; Steel 10; Titanium 12 servings per crock.
mc:handbooktext-watercapacity: Water capacity varies by metal: Copper and Bismuth 7 L; Brass and Nickel 11 L; Cupronickel and Electrum 13 L; Silver and Gold 15 L. Higher capacities last longer between refills. Iron 12 L; Meteoric iron 14 L; Steel 16 L; Titanium 18 L.
